title: Splitting a String Into Descending Consecutive Values
summary: Given a string s made of digits, determine if it can be split into two or more non-empty substrings such that the numerical values of these substrings are in strictly decreasing order and the difference between consecutive values is exactly 1.
statement: Given a string s made of digits, determine if it can be split into two or more non-empty substrings such that the numerical values of these substrings are in strictly decreasing order and the difference between consecutive values is exactly 1. Return true if such a split is possible, otherwise return false. A substring is a continuous segment of the original string.
constraints: Split the entire digit string into at least two nonempty substrings; leading zeros are allowed.
Successive integer values must decrease by exactly one.
hints: Choose the first number length, then every later value is forced.
Use recursive backtracking that grows the next substring digit by digit.
Recurse only when the parsed value equals previous-1; require at least two parts at the end.
The recursion enumerates every possible boundary sequence, and the equality filter retains exactly descending consecutive numeric values, including leading-zero spellings.
